speaker: Unknown
en: Why do most devs not care about writing performance software?
zh: 为什么大多数开发者不在乎编写高性能软件？

speaker: Unknown
en: And should we?
zh: 我们应该在乎吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Today's guest, Casey Moratori, spent the last decade arguing that we should.
zh: 今天的嘉宾 Casey Moratori 过去十年一直在主张我们应该在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: He also says that most software out there runs tens to hundred times slower than it needs to.
zh: 他还说，市面上大多数软件的运行速度比所需速度慢几十到几百倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today we discuss why the focus on performance took a backseat across the industry and why Casey thinks the tide is finally turning.
zh: 今天我们要讨论为什么对性能的关注在整个行业中退居次席，以及为什么 Casey 认为趋势终于正在逆转。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why you'll want to learn reading assembly if you're serious about high performance code and why it's less scary than it sounds.
zh: 为什么如果你对高性能代码是认真的，你会想要学习阅读汇编，以及为什么它听起来没那么可怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: The saying, premature optimization is the root of all evil, why Casey says that the majority of people use it to avoid thinking about performance when they really should, and many more.
zh: 谚语“过早优化是万恶之源”，为什么 Casey 说大多数人用它来在真正应该考虑性能时避免思考性能，以及更多内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to get better at writing faster software and become a better engineer while doing so, then this episode is for you.
zh: 如果你想在编写更快的软件方面做得更好，并在此过程中成为一名更好的工程师，那么这一集适合你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're one of the people who hit a like on this post by Ryan asking for this episode to be more about programming than about AI, this episode is also for you.
zh: 如果你是那些给 Ryan 的这篇帖子点赞的人之一，要求这一集多讲编程而不是 AI，这一集也适合你。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is presented by Antisysys.
zh: 本集由 Antisysys 呈现。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you work with agents, your job is no longer just writing code, it's also specifying and testing it.
zh: 如果你与智能体一起工作，你的工作不再只是编写代码，还包括指定和测试它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Antisysys is the most effective method of verifying agentic code today.
zh: Antisysys 是当今验证智能体代码最有效的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is brought to you by Sentry.
zh: 本节目由 Sentry 赞助播出。

speaker: Unknown
en: You probably already know what Sentry is because you're a developer.
zh: 你可能已经知道 Sentry 是什么，因为你是一名开发者。

speaker: Unknown
en: If not, just ask a dev and they'll tell you.
zh: 如果不知道，随便问个开发者，他们会告诉你的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I use Sentry to monitor the backend of the Pragmatic Engine for any and all events and errors.
zh: 我使用 Sentry 监控实用引擎的后端，以获取任何和所有的事件和错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, Sentry doesn't only do errors.
zh: 当然，Sentry 不仅处理错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also have logs, replays, spans, profiles, metrics, and more because they're all connected to the same trace.
zh: 它们还有日志、回放、跨度、性能分析、指标等等，因为它们都连接到同一个追踪。

speaker: Unknown
en: One new capability Sentry has I'm really liking is its ability to fix errors.
zh: Sentry 拥有的一项我很喜欢的新功能是它修复错误的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me show you.
zh: 让我展示给你看。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's a list of errors on my admin backend.
zh: 这是我的管理后端上的错误列表。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a recent error on auth that I want to check out.
zh: auth 上有一个最近的错误，我想检查一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's have CIR run an autofix for us.
zh: 让我们让 CIR 为我们运行自动修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: CIR is Sentry's AI debugging tool.
zh: CIR 是 Sentry 的 AI 调试工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, it generates a root cause analysis.
zh: 首先，它生成一个根本原因分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's finding some problem with HTTP versus HTTPS URLs.
zh: 它发现了 HTTP 与 HTTPS URL 的一些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now that we know what's going wrong, CIR can create a plan on how to go about fixing it.
zh: 现在我们知道哪里出了问题，CIR 可以制定一个关于如何修复它的计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could go and edit this plan, but I'm happy with it, so let's create the actual code fix.
zh: 我可以去编辑这个计划，但我对它很满意，所以让我们创建实际的代码修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the code fix that's here generated.
zh: 这里是生成的代码修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: Assuming it looks good, and in my case it does, let's drop the pull request.
zh: 假设它看起来不错，在我的例子中确实不错，让我们提交拉取请求。

speaker: Unknown
en: And boom, the PR is created, ready to merge.
zh: 轰，PR 创建好了，准备合并。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I love about autofix is how Sentry went from showing a list of errors inside my application to offering me a fast way to fix it and close the loop while I stay in charge of this bug fix the whole time.
zh: 我喜欢自动修复的地方在于，Sentry 如何从显示我应用程序内部的错误列表转变为提供一种快速修复它的方法并闭环，而我始终负责这个错误修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: Debugging got a whole lot faster and a whole lot easier.
zh: 调试变得快了很多，也容易了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Check out Sentry at sentry.io slash pragmatic and start detecting errors, diagnosing your root causes, and fixing issues and regressions today.
zh: 访问 sentry.io/pragmatic 查看 Sentry，并立即开始检测错误、诊断根本原因以及修复问题和回归。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, Casey, welcome to the podcast.
zh: 好的，Casey，欢迎来到播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so nice to have you here.
zh: 很高兴你来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much.
zh: 非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's great to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for the invitation.
zh: 谢谢你的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I want to go back when we start to the beginning.
zh: 现在，我想回到我们开始的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you get into tech, programming, computers?
zh: 你是如何进入科技、编程、计算机领域的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I guess computers, it's like very, very early on.
zh: 嗯，我想计算机，是非常非常早的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: My dad was a programmer at Digital Equipment Corporation, which is a company that people will know if they studied computer history, but would not know if you just looked at the landscape today.
zh: 我爸爸是数字设备公司的程序员，这是一家如果人们学习过计算机历史就会知道，但如果你只看今天的格局就不会知道的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're completely gone, right?
zh: 它们完全消失了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: They got absorbed partly by Intel, partly by Compaq, I think.
zh: 我认为它们部分被 Intel 吸收，部分被 Compaq 吸收。

speaker: Unknown
en: They kind of got broken up.
zh: 它们有点被拆分了。

speaker: Unknown
en: At that time, it was kind of a really big computer manufacturer, you know, computers like the PDP-11.
zh: 在那个时候，它真的是一家非常大的计算机制造商，你知道，像 PDP-11 这样的计算机。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a Digital Equipment Corporation computer.
zh: 那是一台数字设备公司的计算机。

speaker: Unknown
en: The VAX, like things that you may have heard of in computer history.
zh: VAX，像你可能在计算机历史中听到过的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, these were these massive mainframes.
zh: 哦，这些是那些大型机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, mini computers as well.
zh: 是的，还有小型机。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like smaller also sometimes than mainframes, like the kind of next step down, right?
zh: 所以有时候也比大型机小，就像是低一个档次的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in general, that era, my dad was a programmer there.
zh: 所以总的来说，那个时代，我爸爸是那的一名程序员。

speaker: Unknown
en: He would later end up at Intel because, you know, like I said, parts got acquired.
zh: 他后来会去到 Intel，因为，你知道，就像我说的，部分业务被收购了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He never actually left his job.
zh: 他其实从未离开过他的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: He just ended up at Intel through kind of digital's eventual demise.
zh: 他只是通过 Digital 最终的消亡去了 Intel。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as a result, we always had computers at home, even though at that time, you know, that might've been a little bit odd.
zh: 但结果就是，我们在家总是有电脑，尽管在那个时候，你知道，那可能有点奇怪。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I learned a program when I was seven, which would have been in like, you know, 1982 or something like that.
zh: 你知道，我七岁就学习了编程，那应该是在像，你知道，1982 年或大概那个时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so at that time, you know, maybe you might have an Apple or Commodore kind of computer at home, like some kind of early computer.
zh: 所以那个时候，你知道，也许你家里会有一台 Apple 或 Commodore 之类的电脑，像某种早期的电脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't remember the exact dates of those computers, but most people didn't.
zh: 我不记得那些电脑的确切日期，但大多数人都 没。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was only until a little bit later that you would, and you probably wouldn't have had a programmer in your household to teach you, more importantly, right?
zh: 直到稍微晚一点你才会，而且更重要的是，你可能家里没有程序员来教你，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I learned really early on, and that's when I got into computers.
zh: 所以我很早就学了，那就是我进入计算机领域的 时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: How I got into games was I ended up randomly interning at Microsoft, and I met people there, and I went and sort of went off into games through them.
zh: 我进入游戏领域的 原因是我最终随机地在 Microsoft 实习，我在那里认识了人，然后我通过他们有点偏离进入了游戏领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was how that happened, if that makes sense.
zh: 事情就是这样发生的，如果这说得通的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But wait, how is the Microsoft slash games relationship?
zh: 但是等等，Microsoft 和游戏的关系是怎样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not kind of a given, right?
zh: 这不是理所当然的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Microsoft is not...
zh: Microsoft 不是……

speaker: Unknown
en: They have one game, right?
zh: 他们只有一个游戏，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's Flight Simulator.
zh: 是 Flight Simulator。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, at that time, it would have been very weird.
zh: 是的，在那个时候，那会很奇怪。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason that happened was a guy called Chris Hecker, who a lot of people don't really know his history because there was sort of two waves of bringing games to Microsoft Windows.
zh: 发生的原因是有一个叫 Chris Hecker 的人，很多人不太了解他的历史，因为把游戏带到 Microsoft Windows 大概有两波浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's funny to think about now because people think of like, what platform are you going to play games on if you have a PC?
zh: 现在想起来很有趣，因为人们会想，比如，如果你有 PC，你会在什么平台上玩游戏？

speaker: Unknown
en: Windows is like the default.
zh: Windows 就像是默认的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Linux is now an insurgent to that, but Windows is the default.
zh: Linux 现在对此来说是个挑战者，但 Windows 是默认的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you think about how did that happen?
zh: 所以你会想这是怎么发生的？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, because that wasn't the case if you were back in the early days.
zh: 你知道，因为如果你回到早期的话，情况并非如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Microsoft Windows, not a gaming platform.
zh: Microsoft Windows，不是游戏平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's almost nothing on it.
zh: 它上面几乎什么都没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like Solitaire and Minesweeper and a few other sort of games.
zh: 像 Solitaire（纸牌）和 Minesweeper（扫雷）以及其他几类游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did that happen?
zh: 那是怎么发生的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So what happened, the reason for this, this kind of gets into a technological reason.
zh: 所以发生了什么，这其中的原因，这有点涉及到技术原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason for this is that it was very hard to actually produce images that could be displayed on the screen quickly.
zh: 原因是，很难实际生成能够快速显示在屏幕上的图像。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to understand why this is, is like its own kind of topic.
zh: 要理解为什么，就像是一个独立的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in general, you can just imagine you have this operating system running, which is Microsoft Windows.
zh: 但总的来说，你可以想象你有这个操作系统在运行，它是 Microsoft Windows。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's controlling the graphics card.
zh: 它正在控制显卡。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's often running at a fairly high resolution compared to what a game might want to run at.
zh: 它通常以相当高的分辨率运行，相比于游戏可能想要运行的分辨率。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to negotiate with it in order to display your bitmap in some way that won't destroy all the things that it's trying to display, so on and so forth.
zh: 你必须与它协商，以便以某种不会破坏它试图显示的所有东西的方式显示你的位图，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Early versions of Windows up through like Windows 3, Windows for Workgroups, let's say, if anyone remembers that name.
zh: Windows 的早期版本，直到像 Windows 3、Windows for Workgroups，比方说，如果有人记得那个名字的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was that after 3.1?
zh: 那是在 3.1 之后吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was 3.51, I think is what it was called.
zh: 我想它叫 3.51。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or maybe just 3.1.
zh: 或者可能只是 3.1。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, there's NT 3.51, no.
zh: 是的，有 NT 3.51，不。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like, I think you're right, 3.1, 3.1, I don't know, something like this.
zh: 所以就像，我想你是对的，3.1，3.1，我不知道，像这样之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Windows for Workgroups was around that time.
zh: Windows for Workgroups 大约在那个时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: That version of Windows...
zh: 那个版本的 Windows……

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is in the three series didn't really have a way to quickly use the CPU to fill pixels, which is what games need to do, right?
zh: 它是三系列的，并没有真正有一种方法来快速使用 CPU 填充像素，这是游戏需要做的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no GPU acceleration really at this point.
zh: 这时候真的没有 GPU 加速。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a little bit we could talk about, but it's not mainstream.
zh: 有一点点我们可以谈论的，但它不是主流。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not in consumer.
zh: 它不在消费级。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they need to be able to do this sort of thing.
zh: 所以他们需要能够做这种事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They need to do it in a double buffered way so they can draw to a back buffer and then show it to the screen.
zh: 他们需要以双缓冲的方式来做，以便他们可以绘制到后缓冲区，然后将其展示到屏幕上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that has to happen very quickly.
zh: 而且这必须发生得非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there just wasn't a way to do this in Windows.
zh: 而在 Windows 中根本没有办法做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: In Windows, you had to kind of go through this API where you would produce sort of a...
zh: 在 Windows 中，你必须得通过这个 API，在那里你会产生一种……

speaker: Unknown
en: Bitmap that wasn't necessarily in the right format for the display you were using, and then it had to do a translation from that bitmap to the other one when it displayed it, all this sort of stuff.
zh: 位图，它不一定是你正在使用的显示器的正确格式，然后它必须在显示时进行从那个位图到另一个位图的转换，所有这类事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So games on Windows, like things like Doom, they're not coming to Windows, right?
zh: 所以 Windows 上的游戏，像 Doom 之类的东西，它们不会来到 Windows 上，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That kind of future was not in the works.
zh: 那种未来并不在计划之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: For Windows.
zh: 对于 Windows 而言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was kind of what some people in Microsoft wanted to change.
zh: 这大概就是微软的一些人想要改变的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the people who brought this change about was a guy named Chris Hecker.
zh: 而促成这一改变的人之一是一个叫 Chris Hecker 的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he was like, okay, we could actually just make a library that did the fast blitz to the screen so that we could have a way that people could do these draws and get them on the screen quick enough to make gaming viable.
zh: 他就像，好吧，我们实际上可以做一个库，它能快速 blitz 到屏幕，这样我们就有一种方法，让人们可以做这些绘制并把它们足够快地弄到屏幕上，使游戏成为可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would it be 100% as fast as DOS?
zh: 它能有 DOS 那么快 100% 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably not, but could you actually run some of these new games?
zh: 可能不会，但你实际上能运行一些这些新游戏吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, Wolfenstein 3D, I think, would have been out at this time.
zh: 你知道，Wolfenstein 3D，我想，那时应该已经发布了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Doom was kind of on the horizon and that sort of thing, right?
zh: Doom 当时有点即将来临，那一类事情，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he started this project that he was not supposed to do, he did not have the authority to do this, called WinG, which at least stands for Win Graphics or something like that.
zh: 所以他启动了他不应该做的这个项目，他没有权做这个，叫作 WinG，它至少代表 Win Graphics 或类似的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Total Skunk Works Project.
zh: 完全的臭鼬工厂项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had cover from his manager.
zh: 他有他经理的掩护。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm assuming I can say all this stuff now because it's ancient history.
zh: 我假设我现在可以说所有这些事情，因为这都是陈年往事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had cover from his manager.
zh: 他有他经理的掩护。

speaker: Unknown
en: The guy's name was Michael Edwards.
zh: 那家伙的名字是 Michael Edwards。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Michael Edwards basically just kind of ran cover for this, which is a thing that probably wasn't going to fly because they were in a division at that time, which would have been Microsoft Research today.
zh: Michael Edwards 基本上就是为此做掩护，而这是一件大概不会成功的事情，因为他们当时在一个部门，那在今天就是微软研究院。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was called AT, Advanced Technology.
zh: 它叫作 AT，Advanced Technology。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was the early version of Microsoft Research.
zh: 它是微软研究院的早期版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were not supposed to be shipping core libraries for Windows.
zh: 你不应该为 Windows 发布核心库。

speaker: Unknown
en: It had nothing to do with that.
zh: 那跟这毫无关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Long story long, what ended up happening is that product did ship.
zh: 长话长说，最终发生的事情是那个产品确实发布了。

speaker: Unknown
en: WinG, I guess you wouldn't call it a product.
zh: WinG，我想你不会叫它产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an add-on for Windows.
zh: 它是 Windows 的一个附加组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It did ship, and it was the first step towards DirectX.
zh: 它确实发布了，它是通往 DirectX 的第一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: People forget that.
zh: 人们忘记了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: WinG was the first way you did this.
zh: WinG 是你做这件事的第一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then eventually we had DirectX and Dibsections and Win95 and all that sort of stuff.
zh: 然后最终我们有了 DirectX 和 Dibsections 以及 Win95 和所有那类东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I went to Microsoft, amusingly, the person I was supposed to be reporting to as an intern was Michael Edwards.
zh: 当我去微软时，有趣的是，我作为实习生本该向他汇报的人是 Michael Edwards。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I showed up, first day, along with the other interns, a guy named Rudy, a guy named Rajiv, we were all supposed to report to him, right, because you get a couple interns under one, you know, sort of manager.
zh: 当我出现时，第一天，和其他实习生一起，一个叫 Rudy 的人，一个叫 Rajiv 的人，我们都本该向他汇报，对吧，因为你在一个，你知道，某种经理手下会有几个实习生。

speaker: Unknown
en: We show up and we're just taken aside, you know, after some kind of, you know, stupid HR orientation thing that was, you know, lame as it always is.
zh: 我们出现了然后我们只是被带到一边，你知道，在某种，你知道，愚蠢的人力资源入职介绍之后，那事情，你知道，像往常一样蹩脚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we get taken aside by somebody, I don't remember this, they're like, look, bit of a problem.
zh: 然后我们被某个人带到一边，我不记得这个了，他们就像，看，有点问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Uh, the person you interviewed with and were supposed to, like, report to, uh, they, they aren't here.

zh: 人们对代码如何工作有很多奇怪的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just go do this testing.
zh: 你可以直接去进行这个测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you have lots of these little functions, if they're all statically defined and aren't virtual calls, if they're just known calls, or just member functions.
zh: 当你有很多这些小函数时，如果它们都是静态定义的且不是虚函数调用，如果它们只是已知的调用，或者只是成员函数。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I say static, I kind of mean just known to the translation unit, not external.
zh: 当我说静态时，我有点意思就是只对翻译单元已知，不是外部的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The compiler can put those together, collapse all of the redundant code, and actually produce something reasonable that will run pretty fast.
zh: 编译器可以把那些放在一起，折叠所有冗余代码，并实际产生合理的东西，运行得相当快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Out of that, it can also do things like widen the code path if it needs to vectorize to like run in SIMD and stuff.
zh: 在此基础上，它还可以做诸如加宽代码路径之类的事情，如果它需要向量化以像在 SIMD 中运行之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The compiler has all these options to take what is fundamentally not particularly great code in terms of how you would want it to run at runtime, but it might be able to turn it into that because, you know, compiler optimizing, optimizing compilers are pretty heroic these days and the sorts of things they can do.
zh: 编译器有所有这些选项来获取基本上不是特别好的代码，就你在运行时希望它运行的方式而言，但它可能能够把它变成那样，因为，你知道，编译器优化，优化编译器这些日子相当英勇，以及它们能做的事情的种类。

speaker: Unknown
en: If instead you use all of these things that were recommended, you completely block out the compiler from being able to do those things.
zh: 相反，如果你使用所有这些被推荐的东西，你就完全阻止了编译器做那些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if it can't tell what it's doing at runtime, if it has to leave open the possibility that you substituted in a different class here or something like that,
zh: 因为如果它无法判断它在运行时在做什么，如果它必须留出这种可能性，即你在这里替换了一个不同的类或类似的事情，

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you end up in a situation where the compiler can't do any of that work.
zh: 那么你最终会陷入一种编译器无法做任何那种工作的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people mistakenly think that this is just because virtual function calls cost too much or something like that.
zh: 而且人们错误地认为这只是因为虚函数调用花费太多或类似的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not what it is.
zh: 事实并非如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not the cost of the virtual function call.
zh: 这不是虚函数调用的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could talk about that as a separate thing, because you can analyze that cost as well.
zh: 我们可以作为一个单独的事情来谈论它，因为你也可以分析那个成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't have much to do with specifically whether it's virtual or not.
zh: 它与它具体是不是虚函数没有太大关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has to do with a lot of things like branch prediction and how much stuff was getting pushed in the stack and whatever else, right?
zh: 它与很多事情有关，比如分支预测以及有多少东西被压入堆栈以及其他任何东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's the cost of the compiler not being able to do any optimizations.
zh: 但这是编译器无法进行任何优化的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the actual cost.
zh: 这才是实际的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that cost can be severe.
zh: 那个成本可能是严重的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I showed only, I think, a pretty mild degradation compared to what you would actually see in production if you really had a huge number of things doing this.
zh: 我想我只展示了一个相当轻微的退化，相比你如果在生产环境中实际看到的，如果你真的有大量的东西在做这件事的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it landed pretty well.
zh: 我认为它反响相当不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's a very widely viewed video and a lot of people seem to really like it.
zh: 你知道，这是一个观看次数非常多的视频，很多人似乎真的很喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought it would be, you know, probably even more controversial than it was.
zh: 我原以为它会是，你知道，可能比实际情况更具争议性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was pleased with that.
zh: 所以我很高兴。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I mean, all that stuff remains true today, I guess is what I'd say.
zh: 但是是的，我的意思是，所有这些东西在今天仍然是正确的，我想这就是我想说的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's good for people to hear because they need to hear opposing viewpoints.
zh: 我认为人们听到它是好事，因为他们需要听到对立的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can write code that is maintainable and easy to read.
zh: 我认为你可以编写可维护且易于阅读的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think you have to do those things, so I think it's worth exploring other options that are still maintainable, that are good code, but that allow the compiler to do the right thing.
zh: 我不认为你必须做那些事情，所以我认为值得探索其他仍然可维护的、是好的代码的选择，但允许编译器做正确的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is your take on test-driven development?
zh: 你对测试驱动开发有什么看法？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, when you write the tests first, then you write the business logic.
zh: 你知道，当你先写测试，然后写业务逻辑时。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've talked a little bit about this as well, because it's a practice that used to be super popular in the, you know, like, especially when you're building services, some of those things, especially in the 2000s, kind of got a little bit out of fashion.
zh: 你也谈过一点这方面，因为这是一种曾经超级流行的做法，你知道，就像，特别是当你构建服务时，其中一些事情，特别是在 2000 年代，有点过时了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now it's unclear if it'll come back or not with agents or not.
zh: 现在还不清楚它是否会随着智能体回来或者不回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't have that much of a spicy take on that one.
zh: 我在那方面没有那么多激进的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: My take is very pragmatic, which is that if you can identify tests that will save time in total, that's usually what I try to emphasize.
zh: 我的观点是非常务实的，那就是如果你能识别出总共能节省时间的测试，这通常是我试图强调的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, if the amount of time it takes to create and maintain the tests will actually save us total development time because they will identify bugs that would be hard for us to find in production or in...
zh: 换句话说，如果创建和维护测试所需的时间实际上能节省我们的总开发时间，因为它们会识别出我们在生产环境中很难发现的错误，或者……

speaker: Unknown
en: Or it would be very costly to get to if they got out.
zh: 或者如果它们漏出去了，找起来的代价会很高。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then great.
zh: 那就很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've used them before.
zh: 我以前也用过它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I talked about working at Rad Game Tools.
zh: 就像我在 Rad Game Tools 工作时谈到的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a regression tester that I ran on like the core libraries there that I had written for the, you know, they're not called libraries, but the core like routines to make sure that, you know, anything that I could be testing for our customers, I sort of was.
zh: 我有一个回归测试器，我在那里的核心库上运行，我为，你知道，它们不叫库，而是核心例程写的东西，以确保，你知道，任何我可以为客户测试的东西，我都在某种程度上测试了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think there's good times for testing.
zh: 所以我认为有适合测试的好时机。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say the part that I don't like about test-driven development is the test-driven part.
zh: 我想说关于测试驱动开发我不喜欢的部分是“测试驱动”这部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think development should ever be driven by tests.
zh: 我不认为开发应该由测试驱动。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think tests are a thing that you should be aware of.
zh: 我认为测试是你应该意识到的一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should know what your options are for testing and you should make intelligent engineering decisions about tests.
zh: 你应该知道你有哪些测试选项，你应该对测试做出明智的工程决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, could that decision be that for this particular project, we are going to drive it primarily from the tests?
zh: 现在，那个决定可能是对于这个特定的项目，我们要主要从测试来驱动它吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, that could be a decision that you make, but you shouldn't really think of development as something that is primarily test-driven like by default, because that might be a very bad decision for some other project where it just ends up costing you more to have done it that way.
zh: 是的，那可能是你做出的一个决定，但你真的不应该把开发看作是默认情况下主要是测试驱动的东西，因为对于其他一些项目来说，那可能是一个非常糟糕的决定，那样做最终只会让你付出更多代价。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like with most things, I would advocate for a pragmatic approach to testing.
zh: 所以像大多数事情一样，我主张对测试采取务实的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should understand the cost of testing.
zh: 你应该理解测试的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: The cost of developing, maintaining the test and the cost to your code base if it makes it harder to change your code base because tests have to be rewritten and you therefore don't make changes you should make.
zh: 开发、维护测试的成本，以及如果它使你的代码库更难改变而对代码库造成的成本，因为测试必须被重写，因此你就不做出你应该做的改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of that stuff should be in your brain and you should make an intelligent decision about what your testing strategy is.
zh: 所有这些东西都应该在你的脑子里，你应该对你的测试策略是什么做出一个明智的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: If that decision intelligently made turns out to be we are going to have a lot of testing on this project,
zh: 如果那个明智做出的决定结果将是我们要在这个项目上进行大量的测试，

speaker: Unknown
en: That may well be a good decision.
zh: 那很可能是一个好的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think there's an absolute thing you can say about how many tests there should be.
zh: 我不认为关于应该有多少测试，有一件绝对的事情可以说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some projects probably shouldn't have very much.
zh: 有些项目可能不应该有太多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe some projects should have a lot.
zh: 也许有些项目应该有很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think knowing which of those you are doing is part of being a good software engineer, is I guess what I would say.
zh: 而且我认为知道你在做这两种中的哪一种是成为一名优秀软件工程师的一部分，我想这就是我想说的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned being a good software engineer, but before we get into what is a good software engineer, what does good code mean to you specifically?
zh: 你提到了成为一名优秀的软件工程师，但在我们深入探讨什么是优秀的软件工程师之前，好的代码具体对你来说意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So good code to me usually means that you have written something that is as straightforward to what the machine actually needs to do to solve the problem as it can be.
zh: 所以对我来说，好的代码通常意味着你写出的东西尽可能直接地对应机器解决问题实际需要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also hopefully that you have, I guess I'll say, properly...
zh: 而且也希望你，我想我会说，恰当地……

speaker: Unknown
en: Identified ways of breaking it into easily digestible pieces and named those pieces in ways that are easy for someone to understand, especially yourself, because you are very likely to be someone who's going to have to modify it.
zh: 找到了将其分解成易于消化的片段的方法，并以某人容易理解的方式命名这些片段，尤其是你自己，因为你非常可能是那个必须去修改它的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the way I tend to code.
zh: 所以这就是我倾向于编码的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I try to identify what do I actually need the computer to do?
zh: 我试图确定我实际上需要计算机做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I try to write as simple as possible the thing that will do that.
zh: 我试图编写尽可能简单的能做那件事的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I try to put that in terms that are, you know, I would say least redundant.
zh: 然后我试着用，你知道，我会说是最不冗余的术语来表达它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, I don't want to see, you know, the equation for Euclidean distance scattered throughout my code.
zh: 所以，你知道，我不想看到，你知道，欧几里得距离的方程散布在我的代码中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to have a function that's like compute that distance and I want to use it, right?
zh: 我想要有一个像计算那个距离的函数，并且我想使用它，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I want it to then be nicely broken into the pieces that it represents.
zh: 我希望它然后被很好地分解成它所代表的片段。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I want those pieces to be reassembled properly by the compiler in a way that will produce code that runs very efficiently, right?
zh: 我希望这些片段能被编译器正确地重新组合，以一种能产生运行非常高效的代码的方式，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so...
zh: 所以……

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what I'm usually trying to do when I'm trying to program.
zh: 这就是我在尝试编程时通常试图做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for me, I have never really understood the sort of mentality of there's a difference between code that is like well architected by some principles and code that runs quickly.
zh: 对我而言，我从来没有真正理解过那种心态，即按照某些原则架构良好的代码和运行快速的代码之间存在差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because in my experience, usually the code that is architected properly is also the code that runs quickly.
zh: 因为根据我的经验，通常架构正确的代码也是运行快速的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yes, there is a point where if we decide that something absolutely has to get as close to theoretical maximum as it possibly can,
zh: 是的，存在这样一个点，如果我们决定某件事绝对必须尽可能接近理论最大值，

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, we will start to make that code harder to read and modify because we are now like really over specializing it for this piece of hardware or whatever.
zh: 是的，我们将开始使那段代码更难阅读和修改，因为我们现在就像真的为这块硬件或其他东西过度专业化它了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's true.
zh: 那是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that point is like, you know, way out on the curve.
zh: 但那个点就像，你知道，在曲线的最远端。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not the common case.
zh: 这不是常见情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of the time, assuming you just want code that runs pretty, pretty darn well on most hardware.
zh: 大部分时间，假设你只是想要在大多数硬件上运行得非常、非常好的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: The simple, readable version of the code is actually very fast.
zh: 代码的简单、可读版本实际上是非常快的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's only once you think you need to have 27 factories and 8,000 microservices and all these things running that it starts to be this thing that's like good architecture, but also like hard to modify, hard to read, run slowly, right?
zh: 只有当你认为你需要 27 个工厂和 8000 个微服务以及所有这些东西运行时，它才开始变成这种东西，就像好的架构，但也很难修改，很难阅读，运行缓慢，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: All these things.
zh: 所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I tend to think of like good code, there's like this nice nexus of runs pretty darn well, easy to read, easy to maintain.
zh: 所以我倾向于思考好的代码，就像有一个很好的交汇点，运行得非常好，易于阅读，易于维护。

speaker: Unknown
en: This isn't as close to theoretical maximum as it could be, but it's close enough.
zh: 这虽然不如它可能的那么接近理论最大值，但已经足够接近了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the paths to theoretical maximum have not been foreclosed.
zh: 而且通往理论最大值的路径没有被切断。

speaker: Unknown
en: We left the door open with the way that we wrote it so that if someone really needs to come along and boost its performance, it's set up to do that, right?
zh: 我们用我们编写它的方式敞开了大门，这样如果有人真的需要来并且提升它的性能，它就被设置好来做那件事，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And related to this, what is a good software engineer to you?
zh: 与此相关，对你来说什么是优秀的软件工程师？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it just someone who writes good code or it goes beyond that?
zh: 只是写好代码的人，还是不止于此？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say it really depends on the environment a little bit because I think I've seen a lot of different kinds of good software engineers.
zh: 我会说这真的有点取决于环境，因为我想我见过很多不同种类的优秀软件工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I would liken it more to a, you know, if you want a sports analogy, you'd imagine something more like a baseball team where it's like, what's a good baseball player?
zh: 所以我更愿意把它比作，你知道，如果你想要一个体育类比，你会想象更像棒球队的东西，就像，什么是好的棒球运动员？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's like, are we talking about a pitcher or a designated hitter?
zh: 嗯，就像，我们是在谈论投手还是指定打击？

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it changes quite dramatically.
zh: 而且变化相当剧烈。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there might be some things like, hey, if someone's pleasant to work with and doesn't goof off all the time and actually gets their work done, those are obviously things that we would say are true of any software engineer.
zh: 所以可能有一些事情，比如，嘿，如果某人一起工作很愉快，并且不总是偷懒，并且确实完成了他们的工作，这些显然是我们会说任何软件工程师都具备的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are some general personality traits that might be positive.
zh: 有一些一般的人格特质可能是积极的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you're talking about things that are more specific to just software engineering and not just being a good employee or something like that.
zh: 但是当你谈论更具体针对软件工程的事情，而不仅仅是做一个好员工或类似的事情时。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say I've seen a couple of different kinds.
zh: 我会说我已经见过几种不同的类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen people who are like the utility infielder.
zh: 我见过像万能内野手那样的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're people who just like, they can identify and go and try to fix a problem and succeed.
zh: 他们是这样的人，他们能发现问题，然后去尝试修复它并取得成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if the code base is kind of wacky and out there, they're good at getting the lay of the land very quickly of identifying something that's going on.
zh: 即使代码库有点古怪且离谱，他们也非常擅长快速摸清门道，识别正在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're not afraid to go in and like, okay, this is kind of, this code base is kind of ugly here.
zh: 而且他们不害怕进去，然后觉得，好吧，这有点，这代码库这里有点丑陋。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's okay.
zh: 没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to patch around.
zh: 我要在周围打个补丁。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to do what I need to do and get things done.
zh: 我会做我需要做的事，把事情做完。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a great engineer to have around.
zh: 身边有这样一个工程师是很棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've also seen great engineers who are the exact opposite of that.
zh: 我也见过完全相反类型的优秀工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are just like, I take this one particular problem that we have, and eight months later, I have ground out every last thing there is to know about this.
zh: 他们就是那种，我拿走我们要解决的这个特定问题，八个月后，我已经钻研透了关于这件事的所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes to the point of producing new algorithms that no one's even known before, right?
zh: 有时甚至到了产生以前没人知道的新算法的地步，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That are like these breakthrough things, right?
zh: 那些就像这些突破性的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a great software engineer to have on a project if you're going to be having that kind of thing.
zh: 如果你需要那种东西，那么在项目里有这样一个优秀的软件工程师是很棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I've seen a lot of different people that I would consider great software engineers, and they aren't all the same person, right?
zh: 所以我见过很多我认为是优秀软件工程师的不同的人，他们不是同一种人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that it's kind of important if you're asking it from the standpoint of like...
zh: 所以我认为如果你是从这样的角度来问的话，这有点重要……

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, you need to put together a team to go build this project.
zh: 嘿，你需要组建一个团队去构建这个项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's a great software engineer?
zh: 什么是优秀的软件工程师？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say the best advice you could give someone in that position is think about the roles.
zh: 我会说你能给那个位置的人的最好建议就是考虑角色。

en: Just think about the domain you're programming in.
zh: 只要想想你正在编程的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do a search on Google Scholar for some part of that that you're interested in.
zh: 在 Google Scholar 上搜索你感兴趣的其中一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Try reading a paper, following the references, see what you think.
zh: 试着读一篇论文，顺着参考文献走，看看你怎么想。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a great thing to do and I get a tremendous amount of not just enjoyment from the education of it, but also just like more knowledge about what I'm doing.
zh: 我认为这是一件很棒的事情，我从中获得了巨大的不仅是教育方面的乐趣，还有更多关于我正在做的事情的知识。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 几乎每次我这样做，即使只是为了多了解一点关于事物是如何被发现的历史记录，但很多时候，我就像学习了我完全不知道的全新技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because there's way too much out there for any one person to know.
zh: 因为外面的东西太多了，任何一个人都无法知晓。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而且我不知道……再说一次，因为目前我在工作流中没有使用 AI，我也说不好，但我的假设是，如果你感兴趣，AI 也会非常擅长帮助你找到一些论文来阅读，因为那是，你知道，咀嚼大量的技术记录是它们擅长的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so maybe you could even ask your favorite AI to suggest a paper that you might like based on some things that you tell it.
zh: 所以也许你甚至可以让你最喜欢的 AI 基于你告诉它的一些事情，建议一篇你可能喜欢的论文。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if they're good at that, but I'm guessing that's something they could do.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 阅读汇编比编写汇编要容易好几倍。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 如果你能阅读汇编，你就能看到机器层面正在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而且要理解，例如，为什么像 Python 这样的编程语言比像 Rust 或 C 这样的语言慢得多，当你看到简单操作的汇编代码时，就变得容易得多。
